Who We Are:
Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.
The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on
www.galaxy.com
.
What We Value:
We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.
Seek Excellence.
Be Selective To Be Effective.
Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
Disagree Transparently.
Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
Build Dream Teams.
Who You Are:
You are a seasoned, execution-focused Technical Program Manager who thrives in fast-paced environments and brings structure to ambiguity. You are comfortable operating across time zones and functions, partnering with engineering, product, and business stakeholders to drive high-quality delivery—ideally within financial services or retail-facing platforms.
You own the operational side of software delivery, including intake, prioritization, tracking, and stakeholder coordination. You ensure work is clearly defined, appropriately scoped, and consistently progressing. You proactively surface blockers, drive follow-ups, and maintain visibility across teams, taking full accountability for outcomes.
You have the technical depth to understand how systems connect and where risks emerge. While not hands-on coding, you can engage in architecture discussions, navigate dependencies, and confidently represent technical progress to both engineers and business stakeholders.
You are equally comfortable leading complex, multi-team initiatives and diving into execution details—whether refining JIRA boards or delivering concise status updates. You operate with urgency and independence, and can confidently represent globally distributed teams at the executive level.
Based in London, you play a key role in bridging teams across New York and India, enabling consistent communication and execution.
What You’ll Do:
Act as a key execution partner to the India-based Head of Galaxy Retail (G1), supporting multiple engineering teams (20–30 developers across New York and India)
Serve as the central point of accountability for execution across Retail Engineering, aligning business priorities with technical delivery
Own the end-to-end intake process for new workstreams—ensuring requests are captured, clearly defined, scoped, and prioritized
Maintain a real-time view of team resourcing, priorities, and delivery progress, identifying conflicts, risks, and gaps early
Build and maintain clear, up-to-date reporting (“single pane of glass”) for leadership and stakeholders
Drive structured execution across time zones, partnering closely with tech leads to maintain consistent delivery rhythms
Lead complex, cross-team initiatives with multiple dependencies, ensuring alignment and timely delivery
Coordinate with adjacent teams (infrastructure, security, controls) to manage dependencies and unblock execution
Proactively identify and resolve blockers, risks, and changes in scope or resourcing
Deliver clear, concise updates to senior leadership, including the CTO
Contribute to improving delivery standards and operational maturity across the Technology organization
Embrace and champion the thoughtful adoption of AI to improve team performance and business outcomes.
Leverage AI tools (e.g., generative AI, automation platforms, data copilots) to improve productivity, decision-making, and output quality in your day-to-day work.
What We’re Looking For:
7+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, with direct involvement in engineering-led delivery
Strong track record of leading complex, cross-functional initiatives across multiple engineering teams and time zones
Proven ability to manage intake, triage requests, and define scope and priorities with technical stakeholders
Experience tracking resource allocation across teams and proactively identifying capacity risks or gaps
Demonstrated ability to drive execution—organizing work, following through, and unblocking teams
Highly structured, with strong fluency in delivery tooling (JIRA, dashboards, documentation)
Excellent communicator, able to deliver concise updates to senior stakeholders, including the CTO
Experience managing large, multi-team initiatives with cross-functional dependencies
Ability to engage deeply with technical systems, architecture, and dependencies without being hands-on coding
Operates independently with strong ownership, urgency, and accountability
Based in London, with the ability to bridge execution across New York and India
Experience in digital assets and financial markets, including experience delivering technology initiatives in retail finance environments
Bonus Points:
Prior experience as a software engineer or in a hands-on technical role is a strong plus
What We Offer:
Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus
Hybrid working arrangements
Company-paid health/dental (Bupa) and protective benefits for employees and their eligible dependents
4% company pension contribution
Free coaching and counseling sessions through Headspace
Generous paid Parental Leave
Opportunities to learn about the Crypto industry
Free daily snacks and weekly lunches (London office)
Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues
Employee Resource Groups

jobs.description: At Dow, we believe in putting people first and we’re passionate about delivering integrity, respect and safety to our customers, our employees and the planet. About You and this Role Dow has an opening for a Senior Operations Performance Engineer to support our Polyurethanes Systems House site in Marietta, GA. In this role, you will drive safe, reliable, and profitable operations across production and logistics by applying leadership, technical expertise, and continuous improvement principles to optimize plant performance. You will analyze operational, quality, and logistics data to identify opportunities, validate results, and implement solutions that deliver measurable business value. You will also provide leadership during unplanned events, commissioning, start-up, and project handover activities, exercising decision-making authority and escalating issues as needed to support plant and business objectives. Responsibilities Evaluate and categorize production losses and process deviations to identify performance improvement opportunities. Analyze operational, quality, and logistics data to validate results, diagnose gaps, and drive corrective actions. Identify, prioritize, and implement improvements that enhance utilization, yield, uptime, quality, reliability, and overall plant performance. Lead and support capital and non-capital projects using established work processes to achieve plant, technology, and business objectives. Provide leadership during plant maintenance activities, unplanned events, commissioning, start-up, and project handovers to Operations. Partner with Maintenance, OTEC, and Process Expertise teams to resolve equipment issues and implement sustainable reliability improvements. Support and promote EHS and process safety culture through compliance, incident reporting, and continuous improvement initiatives. Champion operating discipline, effective maintenance practices, and root cause problem solving to improve plant performance. Provide input to turnaround scope development, focusing on availability, reliability, and performance opportunities. Provide shift coverage support during turnarounds and other major plant events. Lead and conduct Root Cause Investigations to identify and address underlying issues. Participate in and/or lead plant teams to support operational and business objectives. Participate in the Technical Team on-call rotation to provide off-hours support. Qualifications A bachelor’s degree or higher in engineering (chemical or mechanical engineering discipline is highly preferred). A minimum of 2 years of relevant experience. Ability to safely work in a plant environment, meet physical demands, work at elevated heights, and comfortably use PPE and safety equipment (including harnesses with a total maximum weight capacity of 300lbs). Must be familiar with or open to training on proper equipment usage. A minimum requirement for this U.S. based position is the ability to work legally in the United States. No visa sponsorship/support is available for this position, including for any type of U.S. permanent residency (green card) process. Continuous Improvement: Applies structured approaches to optimize processes, eliminate losses, and drive sustainable results. Problem Solving: Diagnoses complex operational issues, identifies root causes, and implements effective corrective actions. Collaboration: Partners effectively across operations, maintenance, technology, logistics, and business teams to achieve shared objectives. Communication: Clearly communicates technical information, influences decisions, and aligns stakeholders around priorities. Decision Making: Makes timely, sound decisions that balance safety, reliability, quality, and business performance. Additional Notes This position does not offer relocation assistance. You bring your background, talent, and perspective to work every day. Dow rewards that commitment by investing in your total wellbeing. Here are just a few highlights of what you would be offered as a Dow employee: Equitable and market-competitive base pay and bonus opportunity across our global markets, along with locally relevant incentives. Benefits and programs to support your physical, mental, financial, and social well-being, to help you get the care you need...when you need it. Paid time off for new parents (birthing and non-birthing, including adoptive and foster parents). Paid time off to care for family members who are sick or injured. Creates, provides oversight, and editorially reviews and shapes key messages, press releases and Q&As across the organization for corporate, crisis, brand, and product-specific initiatives, ensuring consistency and alignment with company beliefs and values; serves as a primary day-to-day partner to communications leadership on crisis message development and execution across internal and external channels.

ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X . The Dexterous AI Group (DexAI) is hiring a System Engineer with deep electrical engineering expertise and hands-on experience leading the design and development of electronic sensing systems. Our group invents tactile sensors for robotic systems. You will lead the electrical architecture, design, integration, and validation needed to turn early concepts into reliable systems that perform consistently under real operating conditions. You will stay close to the hardware: designing electronic systems and circuits, reviewing board layouts, bringing up prototypes, investigating failures, and guiding design improvements. Working with sensor, mechanical, firmware, and software engineers, you will take systems from functional prototypes toward production readiness. Prior sensor experience is helpful; strong electrical engineering fundamentals and demonstrated electronic system design leadership are essential. What You Will Do Lead electrical system architecture. Translate product goals into electrical requirements, interface specifications, and measurable performance targets. Make architectural trade-offs across signal quality, bandwidth, latency, power, thermal limits, size, and cost. Design and develop electronics. Own and contribute directly to circuit design, component selection, schematic capture, PCB layout reviews, and board bring-up. Develop the analog, mixed-signal, power, and digital interface electronics that support our sensing and robotic hand systems. Engineer for reliability. Build design margins, protection, fault handling, and testability into the system. Address noise, grounding, shielding, signal and power integrity, EMC/ESD, component variation, and environmental stresses relevant to the application. Lead hands-on debugging and validation. Define verification plans, build measurement and test setups, and investigate failures at the circuit, board, and integrated system levels. Use structured experiments and root-cause analysis to drive corrective actions and verify that they work. Own electrical interfaces and integration. Work with sensor, mechanical, firmware, and software engineers to define interfaces, timing, data acquisition, calibration needs, and fault behavior. Resolve interactions that affect system performance and reliability. Bridge prototype to production. Guide design revisions through engineering validation and production qualification. Partner with manufacturing and suppliers on manufacturability, test coverage, component availability, yield, and repeatability. Provide technical leadership. Lead design reviews, mentor engineers, and maintain clear requirements, design documentation, and test evidence. Establish practical engineering standards appropriate to an inventive, fast-moving team. What We’re Looking For Deep electrical engineering expertise. Strong fundamentals in analog and mixed-signal circuits, board-level power design, digital interfaces, and signal and power integrity, supported by substantial practical design experience. Relevant experience. 8+ years of electronic hardware or electrical system development, with 12+ years preferred. A demonstrated record of leading complex electronic systems from architecture through implementation and validation. Direct design ownership. Personal responsibility for circuit design, schematics, PCB design decisions, bring-up, and debugging. Proficiency with electronic design tools such as Altium or Cadence Allegro, and confidence using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and other laboratory equipment. Prototype-to-production experience. Hands-on experience taking electronic hardware from early prototypes to a manufacturable, production-qualified design, including resolving problems uncovered during integration and qualification. Reliability and test discipline. Experience applying design risk analysis, structured verification, stress testing, and root-cause analysis to improve hardware and system reliability. Familiarity with methods such as DFMEA and DVP&R. Effective cross-disciplinary collaboration. Ability to understand mechanical constraints and firmware/software behavior well enough to define interfaces and diagnose system interactions, while bringing deep expertise in electrical engineering. Practical automation skills. Ability to use Python or similar tools for measurement automation, data analysis, and repeatable verification. Technical leadership and judgment. A record of earning trust across engineering teams, explaining design trade-offs clearly, and driving technical decisions without relying on formal reporting authority. Curiosity about new tools. Willingness to evaluate and adopt useful engineering tools, including AI-enabled tools, with sound judgment about validating their outputs. Helpful Background Experience with sensors, precision instrumentation, robotics, or compact electromechanical systems is a plus. Tactile sensing experience is not required. Candidates from other industries who have designed and delivered reliable electronic systems are welcome. jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The OpenAI for Government team brings frontier AI to public institutions to help them achieve their missions. We partner with government leaders, scientists, and technical teams to deploy AI tools responsibly, with the reliability, security, and support needed for meaningful use. Our Energy & Science pod supports the Department of Energy (DOE), U.S. national laboratories, and the broader federal science community, including NASA and the National Science Foundation (NSF). We help these institutions apply frontier AI to scientific research, engineering, and mission operations through hands-on delivery, tailored enablement, and collaboration between researchers. ABOUT THE ROLE The Strategic Delivery Lead, Department of Energy & Science, will shape and deliver high-impact AI engagements across DOE headquarters and the U.S. national laboratory ecosystem. You will turn customer priorities into practical deployments and sustained use, helping scientists and mission teams apply OpenAI technology to research, scientific computing, knowledge discovery, and operational workflows. This individual contributor role reports to the leader of Federal Civilian and State & Local Government. You will work alongside the pod’s Account Director and Applied AI Architect, coordinating Research, Product, Engineering, Policy, Security, and Enablement resources. The Account Director owns commercial strategy, contracts, and quota; you own delivery coordination, adoption, and customer outcomes, without an individual sales quota. You will lead execution across customer and OpenAI workstreams: define scope, milestones, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and success measures; surface risks; resolve blockers; and communicate progress to researchers, lab directors, and DOE leadership. You are accountable for agreed delivery commitments and customer acceptance. Engineering and Product teams remain responsible for technical implementation and operation of the systems they own. This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role combining senior relationship leadership with hands-on execution. Success requires sound judgment, technical fluency, strong program management, and the ability to turn executive alignment into useful technology in scientists’ hands. This role is based in Washington, DC, with domestic travel for high-value customer engagements, workshops, and delivery milestones. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Build trusted relationships with DOE leadership, lab directors, research leaders, and technical and mission teams to identify priorities and turn senior alignment into actionable engagements. - Own delivery plans for assigned DOE and national lab engagements, with clear milestones, accountable owners, customer acceptance criteria, and measurable scientific or operational outcomes. - Translate research and mission needs into requirements and decisions that engineers, researchers, and senior leaders can act on; communicate progress, limitations, risks, and dependencies clearly. - Connect national lab researchers with OpenAI Research, Product, and Engineering teams to assess promising scientific applications and move feasible opportunities into scoped, supported projects. - Coordinate the Applied AI Architect, specialist engineers, and customer technical teams on architecture, data access, evaluation, integration, and deployment requirements. - Build sustained adoption through practical enablement, user feedback, workflow support, and repeatable playbooks that can be applied across labs and other science agencies. - Lead executive reviews and focused workshops in Washington and at customer sites, bringing the right decision-makers and technical experts together to resolve issues and advance delivery. - Identify security, data, infrastructure, contractual, and resourcing risks early; work with the accountable teams to resolve them and escalate decisions promptly. - Prioritize across a small, matrixed team, make clear trade-offs, and maintain momentum as customer needs and model capabilities evolve. - Coordinate with the Account Director, policy colleagues, and partners on broader DOE and science engagement, while keeping delivery commitments aligned with available resources and approved capabilities.
